script: As stored in the canonical MorphoVerse dataset for this poem -- predominantly Odia script (4 of 5 sampled records, 95-98%), but the Stage 5N audit found one sampled record stored entirely in Devanagari, not Odia script at all (see corpus_language_audit.json for the specific record). Verify per-record rather than assuming Odia script uniformly.
romanization_guidance: Identify which script the specific poem's original_poem text actually uses (Odia or Devanagari) before romanizing -- do not assume Odia script uniformly; this corpus is independently confirmed to contain at least one Odia-labeled record stored entirely in Devanagari.

The Devanagari-block danda (।) and double-danda (॥) appear as ordinary punctuation in genuinely Odia-script text as well -- their presence alone is not evidence the poem is stored in Devanagari; check the bulk of the characters, not just the punctuation.
Represent aspirated and retroflex consonants with familiar reader-friendly digraphs rather than diacritics.
Keep every repeated occurrence of the same source term romanized identically within one poem.
linguistic_guidance: Odia, like Assamese and Bengali, has no grammatical gender on nouns or adjectives -- do not import a gender-marking translation-loss expectation from Hindi/Marathi-style profiles.
Odia uses a classifier system for numerals similar to other eastern Indo-Aryan languages; a classifier's loss in English is a legitimate, text-grounded translation nuance.
Odia vocabulary spans Sanskrit-derived (tatsama) and colloquial registers; a word's etymological origin alone does not indicate this poem's cultural specificity.
cultural_boundary_rules: A culturally specific Odia annotation requires a defensible link to a named tradition, practice, or symbol that the poem's own text actually evidences -- do not add one merely because the poem is in Odia.

Do not infer Jagannath-temple imagery, Odissi-dance imagery, or Puri-pilgrimage imagery unless the poem's own words name or unambiguously depict that specific content -- these are common outside shorthands for 'Odia culture' and must not be assumed as a default backdrop.
literary_context_cautions: Odia literary history spans medieval devotional poetry (e.g. the Panchasakha tradition), colonial-era reformist writing, and a substantial modern tradition -- do not assume a poem belongs to a specific one without textual evidence.
translation_cautions: Watch for lost classifier information (a numeral+classifier construction flattened to a bare English number).

Watch specifically for a script-storage anomaly (Devanagari-stored text for an Odia-labeled record) producing a downstream transliteration side-effect -- document this explicitly per record rather than silently normalizing it.
figurative_language_cautions: Repeated words or phrases used for rhythmic or emphatic effect are ordinary Odia poetic technique, not automatically a distinct figurative expression on each occurrence.
visual_representation_cautions: Do not default to Jagannath-temple, Odissi-dance, or Puri-pilgrimage imagery for an Odia cultural entity unless the text specifically supports it.
negative_confusions for an entity in this language should name a plausible, specific incorrect substitution, not a generic stereotype disconnected from the poem's own evidence.
stereotype_avoidance_rules: Do not adopt a 'every Odia poem is devotional/Jagannath-centered' framing when annotating -- annotate only what this specific poem's text supports.
Do not apply a numeric quota (e.g. 'expect N cultural entities') to this poem -- a poem with zero text-supported cultural entities is a valid, expected outcome.
ambiguity_handling_rules: When a term's script origin cannot be confidently determined (Odia vs Devanagari storage), prefer the more conservative reading and flag the uncertainty rather than presenting one romanization as definitively correct.
When a reading is genuinely uncertain from the text alone, prefer the more conservative reading and use the explicit-uncertainty mechanism rather than asserting one interpretation as fact.
prohibited_assumptions: Do not assume every corpus record labeled Odia is actually stored in Odia script without checking the record.
Do not assume the speaker's religion, region, or gender beyond what the text states.
Do not assume a specific historical period unless the text itself places the poem there.
Do not assume rural versus urban setting unless the text specifies it.
